blocks.text: Named volumes are Docker-managed storage for app data, bind mounts expose a host path you control, and tmpfs is RAM-only scratch space.

rows: Empty volume pre-filled from image path
Copied from image dir on first fill

blocks.text:
$ docker run -v pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data postgres:17
$ docker run -v "$PWD/app:/app/app:ro" rag-api
$ docker run --tmpfs /tmp:rw,size=64m rag-api

Only an empty named volume is filled from the image's files at that path, including ownership. Afterwards the volume's content wins, even if a newer image ships different files. Bind mounts never pre-populate.
tmpfs counts against the container's memory limit; big tmpfs downloads can trigger OOM.

Q: "Volume vs bind mount?" A: "A named volume is managed by Docker, portable, fast on Desktop, and pre-populated from the image on first use: use it for app data. A bind mount is a host path, great for dev source and config, but host-dependent and subject to UID and performance issues."

items: Volumes for app-owned data; binds for files you edit.
Pre-population only when the volume is empty.
